title: You’re knocking… but still living like the door is closed.
paragraphs: You’re knocking… but still living like the door is closed.
Because this might expose something you’ve been hiding—even from yourself.

You pray.
You try.
You fix your behavior.
And here’s the tension you can’t shake:
What if the door is already open… but you refuse to enter?

Not surface-level faith.
Not Sunday-only Christianity.

I’m talking about that silent place in your heart—
where no one sees…
You say you believe in Jesus.
But you still carry shame like it belongs to you.

You still rehearse your past failures.
Still punish yourself for sins He already died for.

You smile in public…
but inside?

“Maybe I’m not really saved.”
“Maybe I’ve gone too far.”
“Maybe I don’t belong.”
🔥 Here’s the truth that confronts you:
Jesus didn’t die to stand outside the door with you.
He died to bring you IN.
“I am the door. If anyone enters by Me, he will be saved and will go in and out and find pasture.” — John 10:9

Not “might be saved.”
Not “earn your way in.”
That’s a guarantee from the Son of God.
And here’s what makes this even more powerful.
In the ancient world, shepherds didn’t just guard doors—
At night, the shepherd would lie across the entrance of the sheepfold.

No wolf enters without facing him.
No sheep leaves without passing him.
So when Jesus says, “I am the door…”
“If you want life—you must come through Me.”
But here’s where it gets uncomfortable.
Because many aren’t rejecting the door…
They’re trying to climb another way.
“He who does not enter the sheepfold by the door but climbs in another way, that man is a thief and a robber.” — John 10:1

Trying to be “good enough.”
Trying to fix yourself first.
Trying to clean your life before coming to Christ.
You’re not outside because the door is closed.
You’re outside because you’re still holding on to something.

Pride.
Control.
Hidden sin.
Unforgiveness.
Fear of surrender.

Not a suggestion.
Not an option.
“I am the way, and the truth, and the life. No one comes to the Father except through Me.” — John 14:6
Here’s the part religion gets wrong…
You don’t enter because you’re worthy.
Jesus lived the life you failed to live.
Then He died the death you deserved.
On the cross, He became what you fear:
So you could become what you never earned:
📖 “God made Him who knew no sin to be sin for us, so that in Him we might become the righteousness of God.” — 2 Corinthians 5:21

Your sin—placed on Him.
His righteousness—given to you.
So why are you still standing outside?
Because entering the door requires something most people avoid:

Turning from sin.
Letting go of control.
Dropping the version of you that refuses to bow.
📖 “Repent therefore, and turn back, that your sins may be blotted out.” — Acts 3:19
You don’t carry your shame into the door.
You leave it at the threshold.
Because Jesus already carried it to the cross.
So stop reliving what He already redeemed.
Stop questioning what He already finished.
📖 “There is therefore now no condemnation for those who are in Christ Jesus.” — Romans 8:1

Not near.
Not thinking about.
Not admiring from a distance.
💔 Some of you are emotionally attached to your shame.

It feels familiar.
It feels “safe.”
It feels like justice.
No more standing at the edge, analyzing, delaying, negotiating.
Say it—right now, from your heart:

“Jesus… I stop trying to earn it.
I stop hiding.
I stop resisting.

Forgive me.
Cleanse me.
Lead me.
📖 “…and will go in and out and find pasture.” — John 10:9
